script: I quietly unscrewed bulbs daily, then their reaction shocked me…. I started unscrewing one lightbulb a day in the break room, just to see if the crew would notice. A week later I tipped over a chair in the same spot, another daily grind, just to test their reaction. Last month they blasted an email about how the bulbs were slightly loose, saying it was a waste of staff time. I felt a tiny win, so I stopped the bulbs but kept the chair shenanigans—because that spot is next to the CEO's secondary office, and nobody ever goes there. The CEO finally sent an email today, asking why the chairs were all over the place and saying they'd come around to pick each one up. No one knew it was me, and honestly, it's the most mild inconvenience I can pull off before they install a camera. I am backing off now, 'cause if they see the camera, the game changes. But that's just the surface. I've been getting treated like a piece of trash for months. My old manager and his boss were best friends, and they got fired for stealing gas. They targeted me, wrote me up for something I didn't do, and then forced me into just one shift a month against my wishes, while everyone else thought I wanted it. I told the CEO about it—he just shrugged and said, "No, they're not targeting you." They threatened us with write‑ups for talking about wages—illegal, right? The CEO sat by and did nothing. The manager got a slap on the wrist, and then he started targeting my friend, making him quit from stress and anxiety, even getting suicidal. I asked for a raise because newer hires were making more than me. I was promised a fair raise, "a little more than $19.00 an hour," for being a good worker. Seven months later, the CEO still hasn't authorized it. I got a tiny raise that didn't even hit $19.00. We were forced to drive a department vehicle that barely worked. The exhaust leaked into the cab, windows barely functioned—felt sick, ignored until OSHA stepped in. The CEO and upper management stayed silent until we had to grab them by the balls. There's zero communication. We never, ever see the higher ups, including the CEO. They care more about tipped chairs than listening to our concerns. The "workers" who screw the bulbs back in constantly throw my department under the bus. They expect us to do their busy work while they sit on their ass and never help us. Complaints are ignored by the CEO and upper management until you make something hit the fan. They don't respect availability. I can't even share a grievance because they're "too busy." The CEO and upper management keep making bad decisions that wreck our department—hours, wages, safety. Honestly, it's the most petty revenge I can do, and the only thing that feels slightly satisfying right now.
